claims: The U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) was established in 1772.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) is one of the oldest federal law enforcement agencies.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service (USPIS) is the security arm of the U.S. Postal Service.
Postal Inspectors investigate over 200 federal crimes related to the mail.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service investigates theft of mail and packages.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service investigates mail fraud.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service investigates identity theft.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service stops illegal narcotics, opioids, and other dangerous contraband from being sent through the mailstream.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service protects postal employees and facilities from workplace violence and robberies.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service identifies and handles hazardous materials, such as bombs or biohazards (e.g., anthrax).
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service ensures the security of mail-in ballots during elections.
Postal Inspectors have authority to make arrests.
Postal Inspectors have authority to serve warrants.
Postal Inspectors have authority to carry firearms.
Postal Police Officers secure high-value facilities.
Postal Inspectors frequently work with the U.S. Attorney's Office, state, and local law enforcement.
The U.S. Postal Inspection Service's official website is uspis.gov.
